findings.evidence: Eye-height view exposes thin isolated wire-like silhouettes and bright distant points. Ground has a coherent cool near/warm middle structure, but geometry does not yet add broad growth.
findings.cause: Verified implementation uses only two narrow strips per instance; projected footprint is insufficient even after correcting the camera.
findings.action: One final B correction: related groups of wider tapered fibres with fewer segments, reduce highlight contrast, retain shared fields and no geometric grass shadows.

review.implementation: Eye-height revalidation at terrain+1.7m, with old ground/new ground/integrated grass all sharing the corrected camera. No change to tree population construction.
review.demonstrated: Corrected view restores foreground scale and confirms broad pigment relationships more clearly; the surface foundation remains useful. Geometry remains inadequate.
review.failure: Two-strip construction too sparse and line-like.
review.reusable: Validate projected scale against camera height before tuning density; record geometry footprint, not just instance count.
review.specific: Dry grass fibre groups require sufficient width/overlap, not tuft cards.
review.humanFeedbackNeeded: No artistic approval; last geometry revision before composition.
